newsitem.title: FRANCE: French left shares ground with Chirac on Europe.
newsitem.headline: French left shares ground with Chirac on Europe.

text.p: France's new Socialist government could find common ground on European economic and social issues with conservative President Jacques Chirac, government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann said on Sunday.

Trautmann said in a broadcast interview the president called for a "third path" last year -- somewhere between a U.S. ultra-flexible economic model and the European interventionist model -- and the new Socialist government's policies would head in the same direction.
"There will most likely be common ground...perhaps this cohabitation will give us a chance to put this policy of Mr Chirac in place," she told Radio Luxembourg.

Trautmann also said the French position on whether to revisit the so-called stability and growth pact, designed to control spending by members of European single currency, was contingent on talks between France and Germany next week.

Asked whether France still wanted to renegotiate the pact, Trautmann said, "For the time being, without this discussion between (Prime Minister) Lionel Jospin and (German Chancellor) Helmut Kohl, I cannot say what will come out of this Franco-German summit."

Ever since the Socialists swept to power in an upset election victory on June 1 there has been speculation in financial markets that their likely European policies could cause rifts in Europe, notably with Germany, potentially delaying or even derailing the single European currency.

During the election campaign Jospin imposed terms on France's participation in a single European currency and while he avoided making renegotiation of the pact a specific condition, he said he did not feel bound by the pact and wanted more focus on employment.

Trautmann said Jospin's position was unchanged to the extent he wanted a "reorientation" of European social policies within a single currency environment but remained committed to the project being launched on time in 1999.

She said there was now room for a clear and precise explanation of what the French government understood by such a reorientation and that it would be an object of discussion not only with Kohl but with British Prime Minister Tony Blair, also due to visit France next week.

With Jospin due to present the new Socialist government's programme later this month, Trautmann said Monday's meeting of European finance ministers in Luxembourg was an ideal forum for France to explain its objectives to other European states.
"What is important is to be able to explain and set out the French government's position to the other European finance ministers," Trautmann said.

"It's an essential step because this exchange is necessary for a good understanding of French policy, and, at the same time the conditions under which, perhaps, it will be accepted by the other ministers," she said.

The Luxembourg meeting was seen as a crucial test for putting the European single currency back on track following the doubts about the new French government's commitment and a row between Bonn and Germany's powerful central bank.
